name: Question 9
problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1$ for $y\ge 0$ and $z\ge 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$
worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/faeecf7ab79009c81daa8a49ddf3c376a7c16acf7ddb4f89d9c00f347eccf2c6.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 1,\,0\le \theta \le \pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{\rho }^{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=1 for y≥0 and z≥0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rz(x2+y2+z2)dV

a
 ∫0π∫0π/2∫01ρ4cos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
b
 ∫0π/2∫0π∫01ρ4cos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
c
 ∫0π/2∫0π/2∫01ρ5cos2⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
d
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫01ρ5cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
e
 ∫0π/2∫0π∫01ρ5cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤1,0≤θ≤π,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=z(x2+y2+z2):

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡ϕ⋅ρ2=ρ3cos⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rz(x2+y2+z2)dV=∭Δρ3cos⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫0π∫01ρ5cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
